easy.def: Away from each other.
examples: The two houses are far apart.
Pull the pieces apart.
The dogs were kept apart.

more.def: In pieces or away from each other.
examples: The farms on this road are miles apart.
The toy fell apart when I picked it up.
The twins sat apart on the bench.

easy.def: A home in a big building.
examples: We live in an apartment.
Her apartment is on the top floor.
The apartment has two rooms.

more.def: A home that is one of several in a large building.
examples: My cousin lives in an apartment on the fifth floor.
The apartment has a small balcony.
Our apartment building has an elevator.

easy.def: Homes in a big building that each family has on its own.
examples: We live in apartments.
The apartments are tall.
The apartments have a pool.

more.def: Sets of rooms in a larger building, each home to a different family or person.
examples: Many families live in the apartments on our street.
The new apartments have a playground and a pool.
The tall apartments on the corner have balconies with flowers.

easy.def: A large animal like a monkey but with no tail.
examples: The ape swung.
A gorilla is an ape.
The ape sat in a tree.

more.def: A large animal with long arms and no tail, such as a gorilla or chimpanzee.
examples: The ape swung from branch to branch.
Gorillas and chimpanzees are apes.
The ape peeled a banana.

easy.def: To say you are sorry.
examples: I apologize for being late.
He apologized to his sister.
She apologized for the mess.

more.def: To tell someone that you are sorry for something you did.
examples: I apologized for breaking his pencil.
She apologized for being late.
He apologized to his sister for the mess.

easy.def: Words that say you are sorry.
examples: I made an apology.
He said sorry as an apology.
She wrote an apology.

more.def: A statement saying that you are sorry for doing something wrong.
examples: He gave me an apology for breaking my toy.
She wrote a note of apology to her teacher.
Please accept my apology for being late.

easy.def: One of the twelve friends who followed Jesus.
examples: Peter was an apostle.
The apostles followed Jesus.
The story has apostles.

more.def: One of the twelve men chosen by Jesus to teach his message, or a person who strongly supports an idea.
examples: Peter was one of the twelve apostles who followed Jesus.
The church was named after an apostle.
She became an apostle for kindness, teaching others to be gentle.

easy.def: A program you use on a phone or tablet.
examples: I use an app to draw.
The app is free.
She opened a game app.

more.def: A computer program that you can use on a phone or tablet to do a certain job or play a game.
examples: I used a drawing app on my tablet to make a card.
The weather app told us that it would rain.
He downloaded a new math app to practice multiplying.

easy.def: Easy to see or understand.
examples: It was apparent she was sad.
The answer is apparent.
The danger was apparent.

more.def: Clear and easy to see or understand.
examples: It was apparent from his smile that he was happy.
The answer to the riddle was apparent to everyone.
The danger of the thin ice was apparent from the cracks.

easy.def: It seems that.
examples: Apparently, it will rain.
She is apparently sick.
Apparently, he forgot.

more.def: As it seems, though it may not be true.
examples: Apparently, the bus is late.
She is apparently sick today.
The road is apparently closed.

easy.def: A strong, serious request.
examples: They made an appeal for help.
The appeal for food worked.
She made an appeal.

more.def: A serious request for help or money.
examples: The town made an appeal for food and blankets.
The principal made an appeal to the students to keep the school clean.
An appeal for help went out on the radio.

easy.def: The way something is interesting or attractive.
examples: The game has a lot of appeal.
The toy has appeal for little kids.
The park has appeal.

more.def: The quality that makes something interesting or attractive to people.
examples: The game has a lot of appeal for young kids.
The old house has a quiet appeal.
Chocolate has appeal for many people.

easy.def: To come into view.
examples: A rainbow appeared.
Stars appear at night.
The sun appeared.

more.def: To come into sight.
examples: Stars begin to appear after sunset.
A rainbow appeared after the storm.
The magician made a rabbit appear.

easy.def: To seem.
examples: She appears happy.
The sky appears gray.
He appears tired.

more.def: To seem or look a certain way.
examples: She appears happy today.
The sky appears gray before the rain.
It appears that the bus is late.

easy.def: How someone or something looks.
examples: His appearance changed.
She cares about her appearance.
The house has a neat appearance.

more.def: The way that someone or something looks.
examples: Her appearance changed after she cut her hair.
The house had a neat appearance.
You cannot tell a person's kindness by their appearance.

easy.def: A part at the end of a book with extra facts.
examples: The facts are in the appendix.
Look in the appendix.
The book has an appendix.

more.def: An extra section at the end of a book that has more facts, lists or pictures; also a small part of the body inside the belly.
examples: The map of the old town is in the appendix at the back of the book.
The appendix lists the names of every plant in the book.
A doctor can take out the appendix, which is a small tube inside the belly.

easy.def: Wanting to eat.
examples: I have a big appetite.
The walk gave me an appetite.
The baby has no appetite.

more.def: The feeling that you want to eat food.
examples: The long walk gave me a big appetite.
She had no appetite because she felt sick.
The growing boy has a huge appetite.

easy.def: A small food that you eat before the meal.
examples: We had an appetizer.
The appetizer was cheese.
A small appetizer.

more.def: A small amount of food that is served before the main meal to start the meal off.
examples: We had cheese and crackers as an appetizer before dinner.
The appetizer was a small salad.
Mom served an appetizer of sliced fruit.

easy.def: To clap your hands to show you liked something.
examples: We applaud the singer.
The crowd applauded.
She applauded the show.

more.def: To show that you like something by clapping your hands.
examples: We applauded the singer at the end of the song.
The crowd applauded when the team ran onto the field.
She applauded the clown for the funny trick.

easy.def: Clapping to show you liked something.
examples: The audience gave applause.
The applause was loud.
We heard applause.

more.def: The sound of people clapping their hands to show they enjoyed something.
examples: The singer received a round of applause.
The applause grew louder at the end.
The audience stood up and cheered with applause.

easy.def: A round fruit that is red, green or yellow.
examples: I ate an apple.
The apple is red.
Apples grow on trees.

more.def: A round, crisp fruit that grows on trees.
examples: She picked a red apple from the tree.
Apple pie is my favorite dessert.
A worm crawled out of the apple.

easy.def: A form you fill in to ask for something.
examples: I filled out an application.
She sent in her application.
The application is for a job.

more.def: A written request, often a form, for a job, a school or a place in a program.
examples: She filled out an application for the summer camp.
The application asks for your name and age.
He sent in an application to join the club.

easy.def: A way of using something.
examples: The application of the paint is easy.
The application of glue is simple.
The application of the rule is clear.

more.def: The act of putting something to use, or putting something onto a surface.
examples: The application of two coats of paint made the wall bright.
The teacher showed us a practical application of math.
The application of cream soothed the sting.

easy.def: To put something on a surface.
examples: Apply the paint to the wall.
Mom applied a bandage.
Apply some sunscreen.

more.def: To spread or put something on a surface.
examples: The nurse applied cream to the sting.
Please apply two coats of paint to the fence.
He applied glue to the back of the picture.

easy.def: To ask for a job or a place.
examples: She will apply for a job.
I want to apply to the club.
Dad applied to be a coach.

more.def: To ask for something, such as a job or a place, by filling in a form.
examples: He applied for a job at the library.
Students can apply to join the chess club.
She applied to a school in another city.

easy.def: To choose someone for a job.
examples: They appointed a new leader.
The mayor appointed a helper.
We appointed her captain.

more.def: To choose someone for a position or a job.
examples: The mayor appointed a new fire chief.
We appointed her captain of the team.
The class appointed a helper to hand out papers.

easy.def: A set time to meet someone.
examples: I have a dentist appointment.
Mom has an appointment at two.
We made an appointment.

more.def: A planned time to meet someone, especially a doctor or other worker.
examples: I have a dentist appointment on Monday.
Mom made an appointment at the hair salon.
The vet could see us at our appointment.

easy.def: To feel thankful for something.
examples: I appreciate your help.
She appreciates the gift.
We appreciate the cook.

more.def: To be thankful for something, or to understand how good it is.
examples: I really appreciate your help with my homework.
She appreciated the cool shade on the hot day.
We appreciate the hard work of the volunteers.

easy.def: Being thankful.
examples: She showed appreciation.
I send my appreciation.
We gave a gift of appreciation.

more.def: A feeling of being thankful, or of understanding how good something is.
examples: She showed her appreciation with a card.
The class gave the teacher a gift in appreciation.
He has a deep appreciation for music.

easy.def: A person who learns a job by working with an expert.
examples: The apprentice learned from the baker.
He is an apprentice.
The apprentice helped the builder.

more.def: A person who learns a job or skill by working for a period with a skilled expert.
examples: The apprentice learned to bake bread by working beside the baker.
The carpenter taught his apprentice how to use a saw.
In the story, the young apprentice helped the wizard mix potions.

easy.def: To come close.
examples: The train approaches.
Do not approach the horse.
He approached the door.

more.def: To come near to someone or something.
examples: The train approached the station.
The deer slowly approached the stream.
Do not approach a strange dog.

easy.def: A way of doing something.
examples: I have a new approach.
Her approach to math is fun.
A good approach is to ask.

more.def: A way of dealing with something.
examples: She has a fun approach to teaching math.
A good approach is to ask for help.
We tried a new approach to the puzzle.

easy.def: Right for a certain time or place.
examples: A coat is appropriate for snow.
That is not appropriate.
Wear appropriate shoes.

more.def: Suitable and right for a certain time, place or purpose.
examples: A heavy coat is appropriate for snowy days.
Quiet talk is appropriate in the library.
Wear shoes that are appropriate for hiking.

easy.def: Saying that something is good or okay.
examples: I got Mom's approval.
The teacher nodded in approval.
The plan needs approval.

more.def: A feeling or statement that something is good or can go ahead.
examples: I need Mom's approval before I go.
The new rule won the council's approval.
The plan was given the principal's approval.

easy.def: To say yes to something.
examples: Mom approved the plan.
The teacher approves of my idea.
The class approved the new rule.

more.def: To agree to something, or to think that something is good.
examples: The principal approved the plan for the garden.
Mom approved of my choice for a pet.
The class voted to approve the new rule.

easy.def: The fourth month of the year.
examples: Rain falls often in April.
Flowers bloom in April.
My brother was born in April.

more.def: The fourth month of the year, when many flowers begin to bloom.
examples: April showers bring flowers, the old saying goes.
We plant our garden in April.
The days grow longer and warmer in April.

easy.def: A cloth you wear over your clothes to keep them clean.
examples: Dad wore an apron.
I put on an apron to paint.
Her apron has flour on it.

more.def: A piece of cloth worn over the front of your clothes to keep them clean while you cook, paint or work.
examples: Grandma tied on her apron before she started baking.
The art teacher gave each of us an apron to protect our shirts from paint.
The cook wiped his hands on his white apron.
